sections.text: White gambited early with 4.Nxf7?, executing a fork on your queen and rook to pull your king out. You took the piece with 4...Kxf7! and stayed a piece up. After 5.Bc4+, retreating with 5...Ke8? allowed White quick pressure, whereas striking in the center with 5...d5 6.exd5 Bd6 would have freed your development immediately.

As the middlegame heated up, White jumped into your territory with 13.Nd5?. You played 13...Kc8? and followed with 14...Rg8, but you had an immediate tactical shot in 13...Qxd5! 14.exd5 Rxe2, winning a full piece since White's queen on e2 was loose.

You set up a pin on White's knight with 16...Bh6??, but it was risky because White had 17.Qh3+, creating a fork against your king on c8 and bishop on h6. Instead, White slipped with 17.g3??, and you pounced with 17...Bxf4! to secure a winning material advantage.

From there, you finished the attack with great precision. After picking up another pawn with 19...Qxe4 and driving the queen back with 20...Rh8, you ripped open the h-file with 21...Rxh2 22.Kxh2 Rh8+, forcing resignation on the spot.

review.headline: A sharp London System unravels after loose pieces fall on the queenside

sections.text: You set up solidly against White's Accelerated London System, placing your bishop on b7 and castling safely. Everything was level until move 9, when you pushed 9...c5??. This dropped protection of your bishop on d6 and gave White a chance to win material. White immediately let you off the hook with 10.Ne5??, but you returned the favor with 10...Nxe5??, which allowed 11.dxe5 and a pawn fork hitting both d6 and f6.

After losing the piece, White stripped your kingside cover with 13.Bxf6 Qxf6 14.Bxh7+ Kh8. White then faltered with 15.Ne4??, allowing your queen into the game with 15...Qh4. White followed up with 16.Nd6, attacking your bishop on b7.

Instead of defending or trading off the bishop, you played 16...dxe3??, which allowed 17.Nxb7. After 17...exf2+ 18.Qxf2 Qxh7, you were down a full minor piece. White quickly consolidated with 19.O-O and 20.Nd6, and 22.Nf7+ prompted resignation.

review.turning_point: After White's error 10.Ne5??, your capture 10...Nxe5?? walked into 11.dxe5, costing you a piece to the pawn fork.
